omar: Heads-up: profiler trace from the edge shows an odd hotspot in http2 header parsing for streaming requests. p99 spikes aligned with increased smallframe counts after the last ingress change.

iris: did we change grpc/http2 framing or our header normalization?

omar: We rolled an optimization that attempted to avoid memcpy for header keys by referencing slices; it reduced allocations but may have increased parse CPU due to extra validation when slices cross buffer boundaries.

ben: That could increase syscall and tokenization work too if it forces extra rewrite passes. Can you paste the trace?

omar: snippet:
```
edge::http2::parse_headers (26%) -> edge::framer::emit_frame (14%) -> host::tokenize (10%) -> host::kvcache_lookup (6%)
syscalls: writev spikes after header parse loop due to smaller payload frames
```

iris: mitigation: revert the no-memcpy header trick and add unit tests for cross-buffer header slices. Longer term, consider a spec-driven fastpath that avoids extra validation when buffer is single-chunk.

ben: for now revert seems safest. Also add metric: http2_crossbuf_parse_rate and http2_parse_cpu_ms.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge/canary -> v2026.03.15-rc7 (pr/4689) by omar. ETA 7m.

perf-bot: perf test added: perf/http2-crossbuf (150rps)

iris: After revert canary shows http2 parse CPU down 18% and p99 back to baseline. Created issue runtime#2023 for fastpath design.

ben: thx, closing unless we see recurrence.
